records.literal_gloss: Let say, please, our lord; your servants [are] before you; let them seek a man knowing playing on the lyre, and it will be, when is on you a spirit of God, evil, and he will play with his hand, and good [it will be] for you.

en.L: Let our lord now speak. Your servants [are] before you. Let them seek a man who knows how to play the lyre. And it will be, when an evil spirit of God is on you, he will play with his hand, and it will be good for you."
en.B: Let our lord give the order to your servants here before you, and they will look for a man who knows how to play the lyre. Then, whenever the evil spirit from God comes on you, he will play and you will feel better."
en.R: Our master, just give the order to us, your servants. We will look for a man who can play the lyre well. When the evil spirit from God comes on you, he will play music for you, and you will feel better."

es.L: Que diga ahora nuestro señor. Tus siervos [están] delante de ti. Que busquen a un hombre que sepa tocar la lira. Y sucederá que cuando el espíritu malo de Dios esté sobre ti, él tocará con su mano, y te irá bien».
es.B: Que nuestro señor dé la orden a tus siervos, aquí delante de ti, y ellos buscarán a un hombre que sepa tocar la lira. Así, cada vez que el espíritu malo de parte de Dios venga sobre ti, él tocará y te sentirás mejor».
es.R: Señor nuestro, solo da la orden a nosotros, tus siervos. Buscaremos a un hombre que toque bien la lira. Cuando el espíritu malo enviado por Dios venga sobre ti, él tocará música para ti y te sentirás mejor».

fr.L: Que notre seigneur parle donc ! Tes serviteurs [sont] devant toi. Qu’ils cherchent un homme qui sache jouer de la lyre. Et il arrivera, quand un esprit de Dieu, mauvais, sera sur toi, qu’il jouera de sa main, et ce sera bon pour toi. »
fr.B: Que notre seigneur en donne l’ordre à tes serviteurs qui sont devant toi, et ils chercheront un homme qui sache jouer de la lyre. Ainsi, chaque fois que l’esprit mauvais venant de Dieu sera sur toi, il jouera et tu te sentiras mieux. »
fr.R: Notre maître, donne simplement l’ordre à tes serviteurs. Nous chercherons un homme qui joue bien de la lyre. Quand l’esprit mauvais venant de Dieu viendra sur toi, il jouera de la musique pour toi, et tu te sentiras mieux. »

sw.L: Bwana wetu na aseme sasa; watumishi wako [wako] mbele yako; na wamtafute mtu ajuaye kupiga kinubi. Itakuwa, roho mbaya ya Mungu ikiwa juu yako, atapiga kwa mkono wake, nawe utakuwa mwema."
sw.B: Bwana wetu na awaamuru watumishi wako walio hapa mbele yako, nao watamtafuta mtu anayejua kupiga kinubi. Kisha, kila mara roho mbaya kutoka kwa Mungu itakapokujia, atapiga kinubi, nawe utajisikia vizuri."
sw.R: Bwana wetu, toa amri tu kwetu sisi watumishi wako. Tutamtafuta mtu anayejua kupiga kinubi vizuri. Roho mbaya kutoka kwa Mungu itakapokujia, atakupigia muziki, nawe utajisikia vizuri."

vi.L: Xin chúa chúng tôi hãy truyền lệnh; các đầy tớ của vua [đang ở] trước mặt vua. Họ sẽ tìm một người biết gảy đàn lia. Khi ác thần của Đức Chúa Trời đến trên vua, người ấy sẽ lấy tay gảy đàn, và vua sẽ được dễ chịu."
vi.B: Xin bệ hạ truyền lệnh cho các đầy tớ đang hầu trước mặt bệ hạ, họ sẽ đi tìm một người biết gảy đàn lia. Rồi mỗi khi ác thần từ Đức Chúa Trời đến trên bệ hạ, người ấy sẽ gảy đàn, và bệ hạ sẽ thấy dễ chịu hơn."
vi.R: Thưa đức vua, xin vua chỉ cần ra lệnh cho chúng tôi là đầy tớ của vua. Chúng tôi sẽ tìm một người gảy đàn lia giỏi. Khi ác thần từ Đức Chúa Trời đến trên vua, người ấy sẽ chơi nhạc cho vua nghe, và vua sẽ thấy dễ chịu hơn."

ko.L: 우리 주께서는 앞에 있는 임금님의 종들에게 부디 말씀하십시오. 그들이 수금을 탈 줄 아는 사람을 찾겠습니다. 하나님께로부터 [온] 악한 영이 임금님께 내릴 때, 그가 손으로 [수금을] 타면 임금님께서 좋아지실 것입니다."
ko.B: 우리 주인이신 임금님께서 여기 앞에 있는 종들에게 명령만 내리십시오. 그러면 저희가 수금을 잘 타는 사람을 찾아오겠습니다. 하나님께서 보내신 악한 영이 임금님께 내릴 때마다 그가 수금을 타면, 임금님의 마음이 나아지실 것입니다."
ko.R: 임금님, 저희에게 명령만 내려 주십시오. 저희가 수금을 잘 타는 사람을 찾아보겠습니다. 하나님께서 보내신 악한 영이 임금님께 내릴 때, 그 사람이 수금을 타면 임금님의 기분이 나아지실 것입니다."

pt.L: Que o nosso senhor fale, por favor. Os seus servos [estão] diante do senhor. Que eles procurem um homem que saiba tocar lira. E será que, quando um espírito mau de Deus estiver sobre o senhor, ele tocará com a sua mão, e [isso] será bom para o senhor."
pt.B: Que o nosso senhor dê a ordem aos seus servos aqui diante do senhor, e eles procurarão um homem que saiba tocar lira. Assim, sempre que o espírito mau da parte de Deus vier sobre o senhor, ele tocará, e o senhor se sentirá melhor."
pt.R: Senhor, é só dar a ordem a nós, os seus servos. Vamos procurar um homem que toque bem a lira. Quando o espírito mau enviado por Deus vier sobre o senhor, ele vai tocar música para o senhor, e o senhor vai se sentir melhor."

decisions.choice: the lyre: a stringed instrument held in the hands
decisions.reason: The kinnor had a wooden frame and strings and was played by hand, by plucking or with a pick. It was played at feasts and in worship (Genesis 4:21; 1 Samuel 10:5).

decisions.choice: music to ease the troubled spirit
decisions.reason: Music was known to calm and lift the mind. The servants hope that skilled playing will bring Saul relief when the spirit comes on him, and verse 23 shows that it did.

decisions.choice: your servants before you: a polite way of saying "we"
decisions.reason: The servants speak of themselves in the third person, as people did when speaking to a king.

decisions.choice: knowing: skilled
decisions.reason: "Knowing how to play" means being able to play well, as verse 17 says.

decisions.choice: your servants
decisions.reason: When the speakers call themselves "your servants" before the king, Balanced and Readable keep "servants", the humble form of address.

decisions.choice: you will feel better
decisions.reason: "It will be good for you" is put as "you will feel better".

decisions.choice: Our master
decisions.reason: Readable says "master" for "our lord", the king; it is not a title of God here.

decisions.choice: tu to the king, with "notre seigneur", "tes serviteurs"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for both books: one person is "tu", the king included, as the Pentateuch speaks to Pharaoh; respect is carried by "notre seigneur", "mon seigneur le roi" and "ton serviteur" (m3).

decisions.choice: tus siervos
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for “your servant(s)” in speech to the king: “siervo” at every level, a polite way of saying “we” (m3). Readable adds “nosotros”, as the English “us, your servants”.

decisions.choice: "kinubi"
decisions.reason: "Kinubi" (harp, lyre) is the usual Swahili word for a hand-held stringed instrument like the kinnor (m1); "zeze" is a local fiddle with one string.

decisions.choice: "watumishi wako" at every level when they speak to the king
decisions.reason: As the terms note: in speech to the king, "your servants" stays "watumishi wako" at every level; "maafisa" is only for the narrator's "the king's servants".

decisions.choice: "đàn lia"
decisions.reason: A small stringed instrument held in the hands (m1); "đàn hạc" is a much larger harp, and "đàn lia" is the plain name for the lyre.

decisions.choice: "수금" for the lyre (*kinnor*) at every level
decisions.reason: "수금" is the established Korean name for this hand-held stringed instrument; "하프" suggests the large modern harp and "거문고" a Korean instrument (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "저희" (we) for "your servants" at Balanced (after naming them once) and Readable
decisions.reason: The officials' "your servants" is a polite "we" (meaning decision m3); Korean says this with the humble "저희", as the English Readable says "us, your servants".

decisions.choice: a lira
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as the English: "lira" names the hand-held stringed instrument with a frame (m1); "harpa", the older Portuguese word, suggests the large standing harp.

ko.B: 그러자 사울이 신하들에게 말했다. "수금을 잘 타는 사람을 찾아 내게 데려오너라."

pt.B: Então Saul disse aos seus oficiais: "Encontrem para mim um homem que toque bem e tragam-no aqui."
pt.R: Então Saul disse aos seus oficiais: "Encontrem alguém que toque bem e tragam essa pessoa até mim."

decisions.choice: see for me: find, look out for me
decisions.reason: "See" in the sense of picking out, as in verse 1, where Yahweh has "seen" a king for himself. Saul now looks for a man for himself, and the one he finds is the one Yahweh has chosen.

decisions.choice: Find
decisions.reason: Literal says "find" here, since "see for me a man" would mislead; the note keeps the link to verse 1.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: As in verse 15.

decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note: the king says "ta" and "ngươi"; this holds for Saul and for Achish through the block.

decisions.choice: Saul speaks to his officials in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: The king speaks 해라체 to his subjects throughout the book, as the terms of this translation set.

source.text: וַיַּעַן֩ אֶחָ֨ד מֵהַנְּעָרִ֜ים וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֨ה רָאִ֜יתִי בֵּ֣ן לְיִשַׁי֮ בֵּ֣ית הַלַּחְמִי֒ יֹדֵ֣עַ נַ֠גֵּן וְגִבּ֨וֹר חַ֜יִל וְאִ֧ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֛ה וּנְב֥וֹן דָּבָ֖ר וְאִ֣ישׁ תֹּ֑אַר וַיהוָ֖ה עִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered one of the young men and said, Look, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite knowing playing, and a mighty man of strength, and a man of war, and discerning of word, and a man of form, and Yahweh [is] with him.

en.L: And one of the young men answered and said, "Look, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who knows how to play, and [he is] a mighty man of strength and a man of war, and skilled in speech, and a man of [good] form, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] with him."
en.B: One of the young men replied, "I have seen a son of Jesse in Bethlehem who is a skilled player. He is also a strong warrior and a fighting man. He speaks well, he is handsome, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with him."
en.R: One of the young men said, "I know a son of Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. He plays the lyre well. He is also brave and strong and knows how to fight. He speaks wisely and is good-looking. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with him."

es.L: Y respondió uno de los jóvenes y dijo: «Mira, he visto a un hijo de Isaí el belenita que sabe tocar, y [es] valiente y fuerte, y hombre de guerra, y prudente en el hablar, y hombre de [buena] presencia, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [está] con él».
es.B: Uno de los jóvenes respondió: «He visto a un hijo de Isaí, de Belén, que toca muy bien. Además es un guerrero valiente y un hombre de combate. Habla bien, es bien parecido, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está con él».
es.R: Uno de los jóvenes dijo: «Conozco a un hijo de Isaí, que vive en Belén. Toca bien la lira. Además es valiente y fuerte, y sabe pelear. Habla con sabiduría y es bien parecido. Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está con él».

fr.L: Et l’un des jeunes gens répondit et dit : « Voici, j’ai vu un fils de Jessé le Bethléémite qui sait jouer, et [c’est] un vaillant guerrier, et un homme de guerre, et habile en paroles, et un homme de [belle] prestance, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [est] avec lui. »
fr.B: L’un des jeunes gens répondit : « J’ai vu un fils de Jessé, de Bethléem, qui joue avec talent. C’est aussi un guerrier vaillant, un homme de combat. Il parle avec sagesse, il est beau, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est avec lui. »
fr.R: L’un des jeunes gens a dit : « Je connais un fils de Jessé, qui habite à Bethléem. Il joue bien de la lyre. Il est aussi courageux et fort, et il sait se battre. Il parle avec sagesse et il est beau. Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est avec lui. »

sw.L: Mmoja wa vijana akajibu, akasema, "Tazama, nimemwona mwana wa Yese Mbethlehemu ajuaye kupiga, [naye ni] shujaa hodari, na mtu wa vita, na mwenye busara katika maneno, na mtu wa umbo [zuri], na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [yu] pamoja naye."
sw.B: Mmoja wa vijana akajibu, "Nimemwona mwana wa Yese wa Bethlehemu aliye hodari wa kupiga kinubi. Tena ni shujaa mwenye nguvu na mtu wa vita. Anasema kwa busara, ni mzuri wa sura, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yu pamoja naye."
sw.R: Mmoja wa vijana akasema, "Ninamjua mwana mmoja wa Yese, anayeishi Bethlehemu. Anapiga kinubi vizuri. Tena ni jasiri na mwenye nguvu, naye anajua kupigana. Anaongea kwa hekima, na ni mzuri wa sura. Tena {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yu pamoja naye."

vi.L: Một trong các thanh niên trả lời: "Kìa, tôi đã thấy một người con trai của Gie-sê, người Bết-lê-hem, biết gảy đàn, [anh ta là] một dũng sĩ mạnh mẽ, một chiến binh, nói năng khôn ngoan, có dáng vẻ đẹp đẽ, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở với anh ta."
vi.B: Một trong các thanh niên thưa: "Tôi đã gặp một người con trai của Gie-sê ở Bết-lê-hem, gảy đàn rất giỏi. Anh ấy lại là một chiến sĩ dũng mãnh, biết chiến đấu. Anh ấy ăn nói khéo léo, có dáng vẻ đẹp, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở với anh ấy."
vi.R: Một trong các thanh niên thưa: "Tôi biết một người con trai của Gie-sê, sống ở Bết-lê-hem. Anh ấy gảy đàn lia rất giỏi. Anh ấy cũng gan dạ, mạnh mẽ và biết đánh trận. Anh ấy ăn nói khôn ngoan và đẹp trai. Lại có {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở với anh ấy nữa."

ko.L: 그러자 젊은이들 가운데 하나가 대답하여 말했다. "보십시오, 제가 베들레헴 사람 이새의 아들을 보았는데, 그는 [수금을] 탈 줄 알고, 힘센 용사이며 전쟁에 능한 사람이고, 말을 분별 있게 하고, 풍채가 좋은 사람이며, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그와 함께 계십니다."
ko.B: 젊은이들 가운데 하나가 대답했다. "제가 베들레헴에 사는 이새의 아들 하나를 보았는데, 수금을 잘 탑니다. 또 그는 용감한 용사이고 싸움도 잘합니다. 말을 지혜롭게 하고 잘생겼으며, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그와 함께 계십니다."
ko.R: 젊은이 하나가 말했다. "제가 베들레헴에 사는 이새의 아들을 압니다. 그는 수금을 잘 탑니다. 또 용감하고 힘이 세며 싸울 줄도 압니다. 말도 지혜롭게 하고 잘생겼습니다. 게다가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그와 함께 계십니다."

pt.L: E um dos rapazes respondeu e disse: "Eis que vi um filho de Jessé, o belemita, que sabe tocar, e [ele é] um valente guerreiro, e um homem de guerra, e sensato no falar, e um homem de boa aparência; e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} [está] com ele."
pt.B: Um dos rapazes respondeu: "Eu vi um filho de Jessé, de Belém, que toca muito bem. Ele é também um valente guerreiro e um homem de guerra. Fala bem, tem boa aparência, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} está com ele."
pt.R: Um dos rapazes disse: "Eu conheço um filho de Jessé, que mora em Belém. Ele toca lira muito bem. Também é corajoso e forte e sabe lutar. Fala com sabedoria e tem boa aparência. E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} está com ele."

decisions.choice: Yahweh is with him: the last and weightiest item in the list
decisions.reason: The list ends with the reason behind all the rest. The same is said of David again and again (17:37; 18:12, 14, 28), while of Saul it is said that Yahweh had left him (verse 14; 18:12).

decisions.choice: a mighty man of strength and a man of war: a brave and able fighter
decisions.reason: "Mighty man of strength" is used of a strong warrior (Judges 6:12; 11:1). David is not yet a soldier; the young man may have known of his courage defending the flock against lions and bears (17:34-36). The description looks ahead to his story.

decisions.choice: discerning of word: wise and skilled in speech
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean sensible in what he says or clever in handling matters. Either way, David is no rough shepherd boy.

decisions.choice: a man of form: handsome, of good bearing
decisions.reason: "Form" means shape or figure; it is used of Joseph and Rachel, who were "beautiful of form" (Genesis 29:17; 39:6).

decisions.choice: the young men: Saul's attendants
decisions.reason: These are the servants of verses 15-17, young men who waited on the king.

decisions.choice: [he is]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words English needs to carry the list.

decisions.choice: a strong warrior / brave and strong
decisions.reason: As in Judges 11:1, Balanced says "a strong warrior" for "mighty man of strength"; Readable puts it in plain words.

decisions.choice: I know
decisions.reason: Readable says "I know" for "I have seen": the young man has met David and knows about him.

decisions.choice: um valente guerreiro
decisions.reason: As in Judges 6:12 and 11:1 in Portuguese, "valente guerreiro" names the brave fighting man (m2); Readable says it in plain words, as the English does.

decisions.reason: Saul's servants must have told him more than verse 18 records. "Who is with the flock" echoes Jesse's words in verse 11: the king sends for the shepherd boy whom his own father had not thought to call.

decisions.choice: Saul sends for David
decisions.reason: Without knowing it, the rejected king brings into his own house the one Yahweh has chosen to replace him. The reader knows what Saul does not (verse 13).

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח יִשַׁ֜י חֲמ֥וֹר לֶ֨חֶם֙ וְנֹ֣אד יַ֔יִן וּגְדִ֥י עִזִּ֖ים אֶחָ֑ד וַיִּשְׁלַ֛ח בְּיַד־דָּוִ֥ד בְּנ֖וֹ אֶל־שָׁאֽוּל׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Jesse a donkey [of] bread and a skin of wine and a kid of goats, one, and sent [them] by [the] hand of David his son to Saul.

en.L: And Jesse took a donkey [loaded with] bread, and a skin of wine, and one young goat, and sent [them] by the hand of David his son to Saul.
en.B: So Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, along with a skin of wine and a young goat, and sent them with his son David to Saul.
en.R: Jesse loaded a donkey with bread. He added a skin bag full of wine and a young goat. He sent these gifts to Saul with his son David.

es.L: Y tomó Isaí un asno [cargado] de pan, y un odre de vino, y un cabrito, y [los] envió por mano de David su hijo a Saúl.
es.B: Isaí tomó un asno cargado de pan, un odre de vino y un cabrito, y se los envió a Saúl con su hijo David.
es.R: Isaí cargó un burro con pan. Añadió un odre lleno de vino y un cabrito. Envió estos regalos a Saúl con su hijo David.

fr.L: Et Jessé prit un âne [chargé] de pain, et une outre de vin, et un chevreau, un seul, et [les] envoya par la main de David son fils à Saül.
fr.B: Jessé prit alors un âne chargé de pain, avec une outre de vin et un chevreau, et les envoya à Saül par son fils David.
fr.R: Jessé a chargé un âne avec du pain. Il a ajouté un sac en peau rempli de vin et un jeune chevreau. Il a envoyé ces cadeaux à Saül avec son fils David.

sw.L: Yese akachukua punda [aliyebeba] mikate, na kiriba cha divai, na mwanambuzi mmoja, akavipeleka kwa mkono wa Daudi mwanawe kwa Sauli.
sw.B: Basi Yese akachukua punda aliyebebeshwa mikate, pamoja na kiriba cha divai na mwanambuzi, akavipeleka kwa Sauli pamoja na mwanawe Daudi.
sw.R: Yese akambebesha punda mikate. Akaongeza mfuko wa ngozi uliojaa divai na mwanambuzi. Akampa mwanawe Daudi zawadi hizi ampelekee Sauli.

vi.L: Gie-sê lấy một con lừa [chở] bánh, một bầu rượu và một con dê con, rồi gửi [những thứ ấy] qua tay Đa-vít con trai mình đến Sau-lơ.
vi.B: Vậy Gie-sê lấy một con lừa chở bánh, cùng một bầu rượu và một con dê con, rồi sai Đa-vít con trai mình mang đến cho Sau-lơ.
vi.R: Gie-sê chất bánh lên một con lừa. Ông thêm một bầu da đầy rượu và một con dê con. Ông sai Đa-vít con trai mình mang những món quà ấy đến cho Sau-lơ.

ko.L: 그리고 이새가 빵을 [실은] 나귀 한 마리와 포도주 한 가죽 부대와 염소 새끼 한 마리를 가져다가, 그의 아들 다윗의 손으로 사울에게 보냈다.
ko.B: 이새는 빵을 실은 나귀 한 마리와 포도주 한 부대와 염소 새끼 한 마리를 마련하여, 아들 다윗을 시켜 사울에게 보냈다.
ko.R: 이새는 나귀에 빵을 실었다. 거기에 포도주를 가득 담은 가죽 부대와 어린 염소 한 마리를 더했다. 그리고 이 선물을 아들 다윗을 시켜 사울에게 보냈다.

pt.L: E Jessé tomou um jumento [carregado de] pão, e um odre de vinho, e um cabrito, e [os] enviou pela mão de Davi, o seu filho, a Saul.
pt.B: Então Jessé pegou um jumento carregado de pão, um odre de vinho e um cabrito, e os enviou a Saul por meio do seu filho Davi.
pt.R: Jessé carregou um jumento com pães. Juntou também uma bolsa de couro cheia de vinho e um cabrito. Ele mandou esses presentes a Saul pelo seu filho Davi.

decisions.choice: a gift for the king
decisions.reason: A person coming before a king or a man of God brought a gift (9:7-8; 10:27). Jesse sends food from his farm, so that his son comes to Saul with honor.

decisions.choice: a donkey of bread: a donkey loaded with bread
decisions.reason: The two words stand side by side, "a donkey, bread", meaning a donkey carrying bread. The same letters could be read as "a homer of bread", a large dry measure, but the plainer reading is the animal, which carried the gifts.

decisions.choice: by the hand of David: with David
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" means "through" or "by means of": David takes the gifts.

decisions.choice: a skin bag full of wine ... these gifts
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the wine was carried in an animal skin and calls the goods "gifts" (m1).

decisions.choice: "빵" for bread (*leḥem*) at every level
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set for the whole Bible: "빵", never "떡".

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֤א דָוִד֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד לְפָנָ֑יו וַיֶּאֱהָבֵ֣הֽוּ מְאֹ֔ד וַֽיְהִי־ל֖וֹ נֹשֵׂ֥א כֵלִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And came David to Saul and stood before him, and he loved him very much, and he became for him a bearer of weapons.

en.L: And David came to Saul and stood before him. And he loved him very much, and he became his weapons bearer.
en.B: David came to Saul and entered his service. Saul loved him very much, and David became his armor-bearer.
en.R: David came to Saul and began to serve him. Saul loved David very much, and he made David one of the men who carried his armor and weapons.

es.L: Y llegó David a Saúl y estuvo delante de él. Y lo amó mucho, y llegó a ser su portador de armas.
es.B: David llegó a donde estaba Saúl y entró a su servicio. Saúl lo quiso mucho, y David llegó a ser su escudero.
es.R: David llegó a donde estaba Saúl y comenzó a servirle. Saúl quiso mucho a David, y lo puso entre los hombres que le llevaban la armadura y las armas.

fr.L: Et David vint auprès de Saül et se tint devant lui. Et il l’aima beaucoup, et il devint son porteur d’armes.
fr.B: David arriva auprès de Saül et entra à son service. Saül l’aima beaucoup, et David devint son écuyer.
fr.R: David est arrivé chez Saül et il a commencé à le servir. Saül a beaucoup aimé David, et il a fait de lui un des hommes qui portaient ses armes.

sw.L: Daudi akafika kwa Sauli, akasimama mbele yake. Akampenda sana, naye akawa mbeba silaha wake.
sw.B: Daudi akafika kwa Sauli, akaanza kumtumikia. Sauli akampenda sana, naye Daudi akawa mbeba silaha wake.
sw.R: Daudi akafika kwa Sauli, akaanza kumtumikia. Sauli akampenda Daudi sana, akamfanya kuwa mmoja wa watu waliobeba silaha zake.

vi.L: Đa-vít đến với Sau-lơ và đứng trước mặt ông. Ông rất yêu mến Đa-vít, và Đa-vít trở thành người mang vũ khí cho ông.
vi.B: Đa-vít đến với Sau-lơ và phục vụ ông. Sau-lơ rất yêu mến Đa-vít, và Đa-vít trở thành người mang khí giới cho vua.
vi.R: Đa-vít đến với Sau-lơ và bắt đầu phục vụ vua. Sau-lơ rất yêu mến Đa-vít, và vua cho ông làm một trong những người mang áo giáp và vũ khí cho mình.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 사울에게 와서 그 앞에 섰다. 그러자 그가 그를 매우 사랑하였고, 그는 그의 무기를 드는 자가 되었다.
ko.B: 다윗은 사울에게 와서 그를 섬기게 되었다. 사울은 다윗을 매우 사랑하였고, 다윗은 사울의 무기를 드는 사람이 되었다.
ko.R: 다윗은 사울에게 와서 그를 섬기기 시작했다. 사울은 다윗을 무척 아꼈고, 다윗을 자기 갑옷과 무기를 들고 다니는 사람으로 삼았다.

pt.L: E Davi veio a Saul e ficou diante dele. E ele o amou muito, e ele se tornou o seu portador de armas.
pt.B: Davi foi até Saul e entrou para o seu serviço. Saul o amou muito, e Davi se tornou o seu escudeiro.
pt.R: Davi foi até Saul e começou a servi-lo. Saul amou muito Davi e fez dele um dos homens que carregavam a sua armadura e as suas armas.

decisions.choice: stood before him: entered his service
decisions.reason: To "stand before" a king means to wait on him as a servant (verse 22; 1 Kings 10:8).

decisions.choice: he loved him: Saul loved David
decisions.reason: The verse does not name the subject, but it is Saul, as verse 22 shows. The love of Saul, Jonathan, Michal and all Israel for David runs through the next chapters (18:1, 16, 20), until Saul's love turns to fear and hatred (18:8-12).

decisions.choice: bearer of weapons: armor-bearer
decisions.reason: An armor-bearer carried the weapons and shield of a leader and fought at his side (14:6-14; Judges 9:54). It was a post of trust close to the king; Saul may have had several.

decisions.choice: Saul ... David
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people where the Hebrew has only "he" and "him" (m2).

decisions.choice: armor-bearer
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the familiar term; Literal keeps "weapons bearer" and Readable says what the job was, with "one of the men" for the possibility of several (m3).

decisions.choice: son écuyer
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the established French term for an armour-bearer, as the English "armor-bearer" (r-en-2); Literal keeps "porteur d'armes" and Readable says what the job was.

decisions.choice: escudero
decisions.reason: The Spanish word for the man who carries a warrior's armor and weapons (m3), as the English Balanced “armor-bearer” (r-en-2). Literal keeps “portador de armas”.

decisions.choice: "mbeba silaha"
decisions.reason: "Mbeba silaha" (weapon-bearer) says what the Hebrew says and serves for the English "armor-bearer"; Readable describes the job, as the English does.

decisions.choice: names "Sau-lơ" and "Đa-vít" where the Hebrew has "he" and "him"
decisions.reason: With both men now "ông" in the narration, Vietnamese names them as the English Balanced does; from here the narrator calls David "ông".

decisions.choice: "무기를 드는 사람" (weapon-bearer) at Literal and Balanced; Readable "갑옷과 무기를 들고 다니는 사람"
decisions.reason: A plain modern description of the armor-bearer's task (meaning decision m3); the older term "병기 든 자" is avoided.

decisions.choice: portador de armas (L); escudeiro (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "escudeiro", the familiar Portuguese word for the man who carried a warrior's shield and weapons (m3); Literal keeps "portador de armas" and Readable describes the job, as the English does.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח שָׁא֔וּל אֶל־יִשַׁ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר יַעֲמָד־נָ֤א דָוִד֙ לְפָנַ֔י כִּֽי־מָ֥צָא חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Saul to Jesse saying, Let stand, please, David before me, for he has found favor in my eyes.

en.L: And Saul sent to Jesse, saying, "Let David, please, stand before me, for he has found favor in my eyes."
en.B: Then Saul sent word to Jesse, "Please let David stay in my service, for I am very pleased with him."
en.R: Then Saul sent a message to Jesse: "Please let David stay and serve me. I like him very much."

es.L: Y envió Saúl a Isaí, diciendo: «Que se quede David, por favor, delante de mí, porque ha hallado gracia ante mis ojos».
es.B: Luego Saúl le mandó decir a Isaí: «Por favor, deja que David se quede a mi servicio, porque estoy muy contento con él».
es.R: Luego Saúl le mandó un mensaje a Isaí: «Por favor, deja que David se quede para servirme. Me cae muy bien».

fr.L: Et Saül envoya dire à Jessé : « Que David, je te prie, se tienne devant moi, car il a trouvé grâce à mes yeux. »
fr.B: Saül fit alors dire à Jessé : « Laisse David rester à mon service, je te prie, car il me plaît beaucoup. »
fr.R: Ensuite, Saül a envoyé un message à Jessé : « S’il te plaît, laisse David rester avec moi pour me servir. Je l’aime beaucoup. »

sw.L: Sauli akatuma kwa Yese, akisema, "Tafadhali Daudi na asimame mbele yangu, kwa maana amepata kibali machoni pangu."
sw.B: Kisha Sauli akatuma ujumbe kwa Yese, "Tafadhali mwache Daudi abaki katika utumishi wangu, kwa maana nimependezwa naye sana."
sw.R: Kisha Sauli akatuma ujumbe kwa Yese: "Tafadhali mwache Daudi abaki anitumikie. Ninampenda sana."

vi.L: Sau-lơ sai [người] đến nói với Gie-sê: "Xin để Đa-vít đứng trước mặt ta, vì nó đã được ơn trước mắt ta."
vi.B: Rồi Sau-lơ sai người đến nói với Gie-sê: "Xin để Đa-vít ở lại phục vụ ta, vì ta rất hài lòng về nó."
vi.R: Rồi Sau-lơ nhắn với Gie-sê: "Xin để Đa-vít ở lại phục vụ ta. Ta rất quý nó."

ko.L: 그리고 사울이 이새에게 사람을 보내어 말했다. "부디 다윗이 내 앞에 서게 하여라. 그가 내 눈에 은총을 얻었다."
ko.B: 사울은 이새에게 사람을 보내어 말했다. "다윗이 내 곁에서 나를 섬기게 해 다오. 나는 그가 무척 마음에 든다."
ko.R: 사울은 이새에게 이런 말을 전했다. "다윗이 여기 머물면서 나를 섬기게 해 다오. 나는 그가 아주 마음에 든다."

pt.L: E Saul enviou [recado] a Jessé, dizendo: "Que Davi fique, por favor, diante de mim, pois ele achou favor aos meus olhos."
pt.B: Depois Saul mandou dizer a Jessé: "Por favor, deixe Davi ficar ao meu serviço, pois estou muito contente com ele."
pt.R: Depois Saul mandou uma mensagem a Jessé: "Por favor, deixe Davi ficar e me servir. Gosto muito dele."

decisions.choice: let David stand before me: let him stay in my service
decisions.reason: As in verse 21, standing before the king means serving him. Saul asks Jesse to let his son remain at court.

decisions.choice: he has found favor in my eyes: I am pleased with him
decisions.reason: To find favor in someone's eyes is to win his goodwill and approval (Genesis 6:8; Ruth 2:2, 10).

decisions.choice: I am very pleased with him / I like him very much
decisions.reason: The idiom is put in ordinary words (m2); Literal keeps it.

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה בִּֽהְי֤וֹת רֽוּחַ־אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל וְלָקַ֥ח דָּוִ֛ד אֶת־הַכִּנּ֖וֹר וְנִגֵּ֣ן בְּיָד֑וֹ וְרָוַ֤ח לְשָׁאוּל֙ וְט֣וֹב ל֔וֹ וְסָ֥רָה מֵעָלָ֖יו ר֥וּחַ הָרָעָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when was a spirit of God to Saul, and took David the lyre and played with his hand, and there was relief for Saul and good [was] for him, and turned aside from on him the spirit of the evil.

en.L: And it happened, whenever the spirit of God was on Saul, that David took the lyre and played with his hand. And Saul was refreshed, and it was good for him, and the evil spirit turned away from him.
en.B: So whenever the spirit from God came on Saul, David would take the lyre and play it. Then Saul would find relief and feel better, and the evil spirit would leave him.
en.R: From then on, whenever the evil spirit from God came on Saul, David would take his lyre and play music. Saul would calm down and feel better, and the evil spirit would go away from him.

es.L: Y sucedía que cuando el espíritu de Dios estaba sobre Saúl, David tomaba la lira y tocaba con su mano. Y Saúl hallaba alivio y le iba bien, y el espíritu malo se apartaba de él.
es.B: Así, cada vez que el espíritu de parte de Dios venía sobre Saúl, David tomaba la lira y la tocaba. Entonces Saúl encontraba alivio y se sentía mejor, y el espíritu malo se apartaba de él.
es.R: Desde entonces, cada vez que el espíritu malo enviado por Dios venía sobre Saúl, David tomaba su lira y tocaba música. Saúl se calmaba y se sentía mejor, y el espíritu malo se alejaba de él.

fr.L: Et il arrivait, quand l’esprit de Dieu était sur Saül, que David prenait la lyre et jouait de sa main. Et Saül respirait, et cela lui faisait du bien, et l’esprit mauvais se retirait de lui.
fr.B: Ainsi, chaque fois que l’esprit venant de Dieu était sur Saül, David prenait la lyre et en jouait. Saül se sentait alors soulagé et allait mieux, et l’esprit mauvais le quittait.
fr.R: Désormais, chaque fois que l’esprit mauvais venant de Dieu venait sur Saül, David prenait sa lyre et jouait de la musique. Alors Saül se calmait et se sentait mieux, et l’esprit mauvais s’en allait loin de lui.

sw.L: Ikawa, kila mara roho ya Mungu ilipokuwa juu ya Sauli, Daudi akachukua kinubi, akapiga kwa mkono wake. Sauli akaburudika, akawa mwema, na ile roho mbaya ikaondoka kwake.
sw.B: Basi kila mara roho kutoka kwa Mungu ilipomjia Sauli, Daudi alichukua kinubi na kukipiga. Ndipo Sauli alipata nafuu na kujisikia vizuri, na ile roho mbaya ikamwacha.
sw.R: Tangu wakati huo, kila mara roho mbaya kutoka kwa Mungu ilipomjia Sauli, Daudi alichukua kinubi chake na kupiga muziki. Sauli alitulia na kujisikia vizuri, na ile roho mbaya ilimwondokea.

vi.L: Mỗi khi thần của Đức Chúa Trời đến trên Sau-lơ, Đa-vít lấy đàn lia và lấy tay gảy. Sau-lơ được khoan khoái và dễ chịu, và ác thần lìa khỏi ông.
vi.B: Vậy mỗi khi thần từ Đức Chúa Trời đến trên Sau-lơ, Đa-vít lấy đàn lia ra gảy. Sau-lơ được khuây khỏa và thấy dễ chịu hơn, và ác thần lìa khỏi ông.
vi.R: Từ đó, mỗi khi ác thần từ Đức Chúa Trời đến trên Sau-lơ, Đa-vít lấy đàn lia ra chơi nhạc. Sau-lơ bình tĩnh lại và thấy dễ chịu hơn, và ác thần bỏ đi khỏi ông.

ko.L: 그리고 하나님께로부터 [온] 영이 사울에게 내릴 때마다, 다윗이 수금을 들고 그의 손으로 탔다. 그러면 사울이 기운을 되찾고 좋아졌으며, 악한 영이 그에게서 떠났다.
ko.B: 하나님께서 보내신 그 영이 사울에게 내릴 때마다, 다윗은 수금을 들고 탔다. 그러면 사울은 숨을 돌리고 나아졌으며, 악한 영은 그에게서 떠나갔다.
ko.R: 그 뒤로 하나님께서 보내신 악한 영이 사울에게 내릴 때마다, 다윗은 수금을 들고 음악을 연주했다. 그러면 사울은 마음이 가라앉고 기분이 나아졌다. 그리고 악한 영은 사울에게서 떠나갔다.

pt.L: E acontecia que, quando o espírito de Deus estava sobre Saul, Davi tomava a lira e tocava com a sua mão. E Saul sentia alívio, e ficava bem, e o espírito mau se afastava dele.
pt.B: Assim, sempre que o espírito da parte de Deus vinha sobre Saul, Davi pegava a lira e tocava. Então Saul sentia alívio e ficava melhor, e o espírito mau o deixava.
pt.R: Daí em diante, sempre que o espírito mau enviado por Deus vinha sobre Saul, Davi pegava a sua lira e tocava música. Saul se acalmava e se sentia melhor, e o espírito mau ia embora.

decisions.choice: whenever ... would: something that happened again and again
decisions.reason: The verbs describe a pattern repeated over time, not a single event.

decisions.choice: the spirit of God: the evil spirit of verses 14-16
decisions.reason: Here the phrase lacks "evil" at first, but the end of the verse shows that the evil spirit sent from God is meant (verses 14-16).

decisions.choice: relief: a play on "spirit"
decisions.reason: The verb for "was relieved", ravach, means to have room to breathe, and sounds like ruach, "spirit" or "breath". When the spirit comes, David's music gives Saul breathing space.

decisions.choice: turned away from him: the words used of the Spirit of Yahweh in verse 14
decisions.reason: The verb of verse 14 returns: the Spirit of Yahweh had turned away from Saul; now the evil spirit turns away when the one on whom the Spirit rests plays for him. The chapter closes with the rejected king soothed by the chosen one, a calm that will not last (18:10-11).

decisions.choice: the spirit from God
decisions.reason: Balanced says "from God" as in verses 15-16, keeping the lowercase "spirit" for the evil spirit as opposed to the Spirit of the LORD.

decisions.choice: the evil spirit from God
decisions.reason: Readable adds "evil" at the start, where the Hebrew gives it only at the end of the verse (m2).

decisions.choice: imparfait ("prenait", "jouait") at every level
decisions.reason: The verbs describe something that happened again and again (m1); French says repeated action in the past with the imparfait, at Literal and Balanced too. Literal's "respirait" keeps the play between "breathing room" and "spirit" (m3).

decisions.choice: imperfect “tomaba”, “tocaba”, “se apartaba”
decisions.reason: The Hebrew tells what happened again and again (m1); Spanish shows a repeated past with the imperfect, where the English uses “whenever ... would”.

decisions.choice: "roho ya Mungu" with class 9 agreement ("ilipokuwa")
decisions.reason: Here "the spirit of God" is the evil spirit of verses 14-16 (m2). Swahili shows this by agreement: "roho ya Mungu" (class 9), not the personal "Roho wa Mungu" used for God's own Spirit.

decisions.choice: "thần của Đức Chúa Trời" with a small letter (L, B); "ác thần" (R)
decisions.reason: This is the evil spirit of verses 14-16 (m2), not God's Spirit, so it takes no capital; Readable names it as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "기운을 되찾고" (Literal) and "숨을 돌리고" (Balanced) for the relief Saul found
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for relief is from the same root as "spirit" (meaning decision m3); Korean cannot keep the wordplay, and "숨을 돌리다" (to catch one's breath) at least keeps the picture of breath.

decisions.choice: se afastava
decisions.reason: Literal repeats "se afastar", the verb it uses for the Spirit of the LORD in verse 14, to keep the echo the note points out (m4).
